title: Hol? -ban/-ben, -n
summary: Countries, continents and most foreign cities take -ban/-ben. Hungary, most Hungarian towns and islands take -n.

sections.text: To say *in* a place, Hungarian adds an ending. Which one depends on the place, and its vowel depends on **vowel harmony**.

head: Ending
Used with
Examples
rows: Prágában, Svájcban, Párizsban, Spanyolországban, az USA-ban
Hungary, most Hungarian towns, islands, “the world”
Magyarországon, Budapesten, Szegeden, Siófokon, Cipruson, a világon

sections.text: A word ending in **a** or **e** lengthens it before the ending: Prág**a** → Prág**á**ban, Afrik**a** → Afrik**á**ban, Velenc**e** → Velenc**é**ben, Lipcs**e** → Lipcs**é**ben, Chil**e** → Chil**é**ben.

After a vowel just **-n**: Máltá**n**, Korziká**n**. After a consonant a linking vowel: **-on** (back), **-en** (front), **-ön** (front with ö/ő/ü/ű in the last syllable): Siófok**on**, Budapest**en**, Tököl**ön**.
Some Hungarian towns take -ban/-ben anyway, e.g. Debrecen**ben**, Egerben. You learn them one by one. Foreign towns almost always take -ban/-ben.
Try it: type a place and choose whether it's a Hungarian town.
